<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/control/codex/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

{
  "ambiguities": [
    "Several generic declarations display 'LocalDef009' as a universe-level name. In those positions it is a universe parameter, not the real-valued model projection D009.",

  ],
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the computed result whose absolute error is bounded in the first conjunct.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For every arithmetic model fp and natural numbers b and l, defines T(fp,b,l,v) for v:Fin(b^l)→R recursively. At l=0, T(fp,b,0,v)=v(0). At l+1, form w(j)=T(fp,b,l,i↦v(j*b^l+i)) for j∈Fin(b), then return the sequential modeled sum S(fp,b,w) defined in D010. Thus each node sums its b contiguous child blocks in index order.",
      "name": "Recursive uniform-branching summation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The first conjunct universally quantifies over all members of this model type; its stored axioms are implicit restrictions on that quantifier.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "The type of arithmetic models constructed in D008: a nonnegative real error parameter, four binary real operations, one unary real operation, exact addition with zero on the left, and relative-error axioms for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and square root.",
      "name": "Arithmetic model type",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the exact error coefficient gamma_fp(t*(b−1)). Under the target's admissibility hypothesis its denominator is positive.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "For every model fp and n∈N, gamma_fp(n)=((n:R)*u_fp)/(1−(n:R)*u_fp). This is a total real-valued definition using Lean's real division; no nonzero-denominator hypothesis is part of the definition.",
      "name": "Accumulated error coefficient",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The first conjunct assumes this predicate at n=t*(b−1), so ((t*(b−1):N):R)*u_fp<1.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For every model fp and n∈N, admissibility means (n:R)*u_fp<1.",
      "name": "Error-parameter admissibility",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the contiguous-block layout used by the recursive summation, including the ordering of child blocks.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For b,l∈N, j∈Fin(b), and i∈Fin(b^l), produces the index in Fin(b^(l+1)) with natural value j.val*b^l+i.val. Its range proof is D011.",
      "name": "Block index embedding",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the index 0 valid in the base case of recursive summation.",

      "name": "Base-level index validity",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Implements the zero-versus-successor branch of D001 while preserving the vector's length-dependent type.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "For b∈N and any dependent family P(x,v) in any sort, with x∈N and v:Fin(b^x)→R, given h0(v):P(0,v) for every length-b^0 vector and hs(l,v):P(l+1,v) for every l∈N and length-b^(l+1) vector, returns P(x,v) by cases on x. It returns h0(v) at zero and hs(l,v) at x=l+1; this case splitter itself supplies no induction hypothesis.",
      "name": "Dependent depth case split",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies all assumptions built into fp. The summation uses the addition operation, its relative-error bound, and its exact left-zero law; the other operation axioms restrict the model type but do not appear in the summation algorithm.",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "Constructs a model from u∈R with 0≤u; functions A,S,M,D:R×R→R and Q:R→R; the law ∀x∈R, A(0,x)=x; and the following axioms. For every x,y∈R there exists δ∈R with |δ|≤u and A(x,y)=(x+y)(1+δ). Separately, for every x,y there exists such a δ with S(x,y)=(x−y)(1+δ), and separately with M(x,y)=(xy)(1+δ). For every x,y with y≠0 there exists such a δ with D(x,y)=(x/y)(1+δ). For every x≥0 there exists such a δ with Q(x)=sqrt(x)(1+δ).     {

      "meaning": "For every model fp, projects its binary modeled addition A_fp:R×R→R, the third stored field.",

    {

    {

      "meaning": "For n∈N, Fin(n) is the type of natural numbers k with 0≤k<n, stored with their bound proofs.",

    {

      "status": "understood"

    {
      "effect_on_target": "Forms the natural product of the t factors and the product of t copies of b.",

      "meaning": "For any index type I, commutative monoid M, finite subset E of I, and function f:I→M, returns the product of f(i) over i∈E, implemented as the product of the mapped underlying multiset. The empty product is the monoid identity.",

      "status": "understood"

    {

      "meaning": "For any index type I, additive commutative monoid M, finite subset E of I, and function f:I→M, returns the sum of f(i) over i∈E, implemented as the sum of the mapped underlying multiset. The empty sum is zero.",

      "status": "understood"

    {

    {

      "status": "understood"

    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the domains of depths, branching factors, indices, factor values and cost counts.",

      "meaning": "The type N of nonnegative integers, including zero.",

      "status": "understood"
